title: Implement a 5-field cron expression parser and Next() (Go)
prompt:
Implement the stubs in cron.go for our job scheduler.

ParseField(expr, min, max) returns the sorted, de-duplicated values a single cron field selects. A field is a comma-separated list of items; each item is `*`, `N` or `A-B` (A <= B, no wrap-around), optionally followed by `/S` with S >= 1. `*/S` and `A-B/S` step through the range starting at its low end; `N/S` means N through max in steps of S. Values must be plain decimal digits within [min, max]. Anything else (empty field or item, out of range, step 0, reversed range, signs, extra slashes) is an error.

Parse(spec) parses five whitespace-separated fields: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12, or JAN-DEC) and day of week (0-7 where both 0 and 7 are Sunday, or SUN-SAT); names are case-insensitive and also work in ranges (MON-FRI). Wrong field count or any bad field is an error.

(*Schedule).Matches(t) checks t's minute, hour, day, month and weekday (in t's location). Day matching follows classic Vixie cron: if both the day-of-month and day-of-week fields are restricted (a field is unrestricted iff it starts with `*`), a time matches when EITHER matches; otherwise both must match.

(*Schedule).Next(after) returns the earliest matching time strictly after `after`, with zero seconds, and true; if nothing matches within 5 years it returns the zero time and false. Run `go test ./...`.
